title: The Art of Argument
text:
An argumentative essay does more than describe a topic; it takes a clear position and defends it with evidence. Its strength lies in the writer's ability to anticipate objections and respond to them before a skeptical reader can raise them. Effective arguments are usually built around a central thesis, which is supported by reasoned claims rather than mere emotional appeal. Consequently, a writer who relies solely on anecdotes risks being dismissed as unpersuasive.

Moreover, the most convincing essays acknowledge the opposing view fairly instead of caricaturing it. Such a concession does not weaken the argument; rather, it signals intellectual honesty and makes the conclusion more credible. Students often mistake assertiveness for persuasiveness, yet a confident tone without solid reasoning tends to alienate readers. Ultimately, the goal is not to win a debate but to invite the reader to reconsider a question.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does an argumentative essay do?
options: It only describes a topic in detail.
It takes a clear position and defends it with evidence.
It avoids any mention of opposing views.
It relies mainly on personal anecdotes.

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what makes the conclusion of an essay more credible?
options: Using a confident tone without reasoning.

questions.text: What can be inferred about a writer who relies only on anecdotes?
options: Such a writer is likely to be seen as less persuasive.
Such a writer always wins debates.
Such a writer is required to cite statistics.
Such a writer never addresses the reader directly.

questions.text: What does the author imply about the real purpose of argument?
options: Winning the debate matters more than the reader's view.
Argument aims to encourage readers to rethink a question.
An assertive tone is the key to success.
Conceding any point weakens a thesis.

vocabulary.definition: a main claim that a piece of writing sets out to prove
to predict something and prepare for it in advance
an admission that a point made by the other side has some validity
to cause people to feel distant or hostile toward you

paragraph_translations: Un ensayo argumentativo hace más que describir un tema; adopta una postura clara y la defiende con pruebas. Su fuerza reside en la capacidad del autor para anticipar objeciones y responderlas antes de que un lector escéptico las plantee. Los argumentos eficaces suelen girar en torno a una tesis central, sostenida por afirmaciones razonadas y no solo por apelaciones emocionales. Por consiguiente, un escritor que se apoya únicamente en anécdotas corre el riesgo de ser descartado como poco persuasivo.

Además, los ensayos más convincentes reconocen con justicia la opinión contraria en lugar de caricaturizarla. Tal concesión no debilita el argumento; al contrario, muestra honestidad intelectual y hace que la conclusión resulte más creíble. Los estudiantes a menudo confunden la seguridad con la persuasión, pero un tono confiado sin un razonamiento sólido tiende a alejar al lector. En última instancia, el objetivo no es ganar un debate, sino invitar al lector a reconsiderar una cuestión.
